name: Caldecott Ironback Motorcycle Jacket
description: A hard-worn motorcycle jacket cut from full-grain bovine leather — real leather, not synth, which is immediately apparent to anyone who handles it. The hide is thick and stiff at first, developing a personal crease pattern over months of wear that makes each jacket unique to its owner. The Ironback earns its name from a wide panel of perforated leather across the shoulders and upper back, originally designed for airflow during long rides but now just recognized as the Caldecott signature. Asymmetric zip closure, two chest patch pockets, and a single interior pocket with a snap closure. Hardware is brushed gunmetal throughout — no chrome, no polish.
what_it_says: You work with your hands, you own things outright, and you don't need branding to tell people who you are. The Ironback is a working-class statement of quiet permanence — the kind of jacket you pass down.
worn_by: people who commute by motorcycle through the corridor
story_hooks: A jacket left behind at a crime scene — the crease pattern is distinctive enough that someone who knew the owner would recognize it immediately.

Caldecott Leatherworks is a family operation out of the old Milwaukee annex, and the current owner is being pressured to sell the name to a corponation that wants to manufacture synthetic versions at scale.
The interior snap pocket is just large enough for a folded document, a vial, or a weapon too small for most security scanners to bother flagging.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions Ironback APC — 'The Pallbearer'

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist statement piece with aggressive shoulder presence. The jacket reads as a relic of pre-augmentation craftsmanship — heavy, sculptural, unapologetically analog. Worn by those who reject synth materials and corpo uniformity. Silhouette is muscular and structured, with the signature perforated back panel creating visual depth and a deliberate statement of heritage.
physical_description.fit: Tailored through the torso with deliberate room at the shoulders and upper back. Designed for layering over thermal wear or light armor. Sleeves taper slightly at the wrist. The jacket sits at mid-hip, exposing the wearer's core. Breaks slightly at the wrist when arms are at rest.
physical_description.primary_material: Full-grain bovine leather — genuine animal hide, treated and conditioned but retaining natural imperfections and grain variation. Immediately distinguishable from synthetic alternatives by weight, suppleness, and scent.
physical_description.texture: Butter-soft on the surface but structurally firm, with a subtle grain visible under direct light. The perforated back panel has deliberate cutouts that catch light. High-wear areas develop a rich patina and creasing pattern unique to each wearer. Edges are hand-finished and slightly burnished.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep cognac brown with natural darkening along stress points and creases. The perforated panel creates shadow detail through its negative space. Brushed gunmetal hardware remains matte throughout, never polished to shine.
physical_description.closures: Asymmetric front zip in brushed gunmetal, offset to one side — a design quirk that signals handcrafted authenticity. Snap closure on interior pocket. No magnetic snaps or friction-fit tech integration.
distinctive_features: Signature perforated leather shoulder and upper back panel — Caldecott trademark
Asymmetric zip placement — intentional design philosophy, not manufacturing error
Two external chest patch pockets with subtle stitching detail
Interior snap pocket for valuables or old-tech devices
Hand-burnished leather edges showing natural color variation
Brushed gunmetal hardware throughout — deliberately anti-chrome aesthetic
Full-grain leather develops unique creasing pattern over months of wear
No brand embossing or logos — status signaled through material knowledge alone
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 crossover. Expensive enough to signal serious wealth or long-term investment, but worn by working-class riders who save for years. Priced around 3,500Φ — a statement that this person values authentic materials over augmentation.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by: old-money collectors, motorcycle couriers in the ungoverned zones, corpo defectors rejecting synth aesthetics, artisans and craftspeople, anyone rejecting the homogenized augment economy. Signals someone who values tactile reality, heritage materials, and analog reliability in an increasingly digital world.
physical_description.condition_typical: Arrives pristine and stiff. Within 3-6 months develops a personalized crease map across the shoulders and elbows. Scuffs and minor tears are collected like medals. A 5-year-old Ironback is more valuable than a new one due to its unique wear pattern. Some owners apply specialty conditioners to accelerate patina.

image_prompt: A weathered Caldecott Ironback motorcycle jacket displayed on a broad-shouldered dark mannequin or worn by a neo-noir courier model with visible augmentation in one arm. Focus tight on the signature perforated leather shoulder panel catching moody amber streetlight. The jacket shows 2-3 years of authentic wear — creases at elbows, subtle scuffing along the asymmetric zipper. Background: gritty industrial setting, rain-slicked concrete, distant neon in deep blues and oranges. Fabric texture should feel tactile and real, emphasizing the difference between genuine leather and synth. Dramatic side-lighting to showcase the hand-finished edges and brushed gunmetal hardware.
